evidence.c1: Power cap, base rate, incentives, flexibility, posterior and triangulation all turn the argument; the 'science can be studied scientifically' assumed idea is near-trivia.
evidence.c2: Every item is a portable claim (e.g. 'a population of rational scientists can still produce a literature dominated by unreliable findings').
evidence.c3: The only assumed idea (metascience is coherent) is stated outright in the metascience passages and is generic, not a local inferential move.
evidence.c4: Anchors fit (x7d5t5, dzsa7e, huxt52, ftd2ng); the triangulation idea quotes the same block twice and heterogeneity rests on qn347b alone.
evidence.c5: Includes incentives and the base-rate argument; publication bias is folded into effect inflation rather than standing alone, and there is nothing on 'failures are science working' or on soft-science NHST.

evidence.c1: Power, winner's curse, publication bias, forking paths, heterogeneity, Bayesian prior and triangulation are all load-bearing.
evidence.c2: All propositions, e.g. 'replication rate is bounded by the power'.
evidence.c3: The assumed 'one fixed true effect' idea names what heterogeneity undercuts (cxbx9m, c08svn, x02d6v); the 'citations track merit' idea names exactly why m3et6t reads as troubling.
evidence.c4: Anchors fit well: k59a2x's 85% shrinkage, q6s08t's fail-safe number for the file drawer, and h7qg2e for persistent low power.
evidence.c5: No incentives / publish-or-perish idea (huxt52, ftd2ng), and no soft-science NHST critique.

evidence.c1: Most items are central, and 'a rejected null doesn't single out one alternative' is a good pick; the frequentist long-run assumed idea is pedantic rather than something the argument turns on.
evidence.c3: The assumed frequentist reading is argued (definitions vs the later Bayesian correction) but loosely tied to m4dued, bnzb3f and sg0nmn as definitions.
evidence.c4: Effect-size inflation rests on hw9d4p alone; the other anchors (j0ubfk, ddw4ya, x02d6v) fit.
evidence.c5: No incentives idea, and the base rate is only implicit in the publication-bias anchor.

evidence.c1: 'Non-replication is science working' (cxcn8h) is a strong pick; the 'trust comes from convergence' assumed idea is near-universal background.
evidence.c3: The citation assumption is precise (m3et6t, x6vcuf); the 'convergence across studies' assumption is generic and its g7w0hc reasoning ('scale presented as a strength') is a stretch.
evidence.c4: Triangulation is also anchored to dtq8wq (multi-lab uniform protocols), which is the opposite of method triangulation; the rest fit.
evidence.c5: No incentives idea and no base-rate idea; heterogeneity, power, publication bias and flexibility are covered.

evidence.c1: Synergy, the lattice, redundancy underdetermination, rich clubs, motifs, the intermediate peak and the task shift are all central.
evidence.c2: All claims, e.g. 'synergy peaks at intermediate, not maximal, input similarity'.
evidence.c3: The MI-vs-TE 'assumed' idea is stated outright in f6sbgx and p4pyuy; the 'firing as a decision' framing is argued but h5dz45 itself states it.
evidence.c4: The redundancy-underdetermined claim (three equations, four unknowns) is anchored only to rc76qn, not bgsd4n, which actually says it.
evidence.c5: No limitations idea (Dedekind explosion, statistical-not-mechanistic caveat); the behaving-primate task shift is included.

evidence.c1: The core PID chain plus the empirical findings.
evidence.c3: 'Statistics treated as computation' is precise (spdx0y read as a late corrective), but 'whole is not the sum of its parts' is stated explicitly in h5dz45, so it is introduced, not assumed.
evidence.c4: Synergy rests on e94ury alone; s0db2g supports non-additivity only loosely.
evidence.c5: No task-dependent redundancy idea (the primates appear only as an anchor), and no Dedekind or estimation limits.

evidence.c1: All load-bearing, including the Dedekind explosion.
evidence.c3: 'Triad synergy is additive network-wide' names exactly the move in fud8q3's 88% claim; 'inferred edges are real circuit relations' uses j4cy9j's caveat as evidence the assumption was in force.
evidence.c4: The q9gytb anchor for additivity is loose ('only reasonable if generalize'); the rest fit.
evidence.c5: The behaving-primate result (task-dependent redundancy) is missing; rich club and recurrence are merged into one item.

evidence.c1: Every item turns the review.
evidence.c3: 'Effective network treated as real wiring' is precise (sw5ukx, xs5660, j4cy9j); 'redundancy as robustness' is in fact stated by the authors in t8fayf, and the b32ecw reasoning is loose.
evidence.c4: b32ecw is a weak anchor for the redundancy-as-robustness idea; the others fit (bgsd4n for underdetermination).
evidence.c5: Covers MI/TE, the decomposition, the lattice, the redundancy choice, the empirical findings, task dependence and the Dedekind limit.

evidence.c1: Intelligence/consciousness, the biases, computational functionalism, inseparability, life, simulation and seeming-vs-being are the essay's spine.
evidence.c3: 'Not checkable from outside' and 'precaution under moral uncertainty' are both argued against specific passages (kqs33c, yverz7); using gwz5eu for precaution is weaker, since it is conditional on actual consciousness.
evidence.c4: Mostly exact (zw2m7u, p4vmm0, un9fjn, npjt4j); gwz5eu does not presuppose precaution.
evidence.c5: No 'other games in town' / non-Turing dynamics argument (gw0hsq, n393ru), which is one of the four arguments.

evidence.c1: All central.
evidence.c3: 'Experience is a fact over behaviour' is a precise local move (kqs33c, p8ky7g); 'moral status tracks consciousness' is asserted in e68t9h and ryg483 rather than presupposed, but is fairly flagged as unargued.
evidence.c4: Anchors well chosen: xdy4fe for the hidden premise in Bostrom, ahtr6e for neural replacement, xk9gne for persistent illusion.
evidence.c5: No non-algorithmic dynamics / 'other games' argument.

evidence.c1: Mostly core; the exponential-curve illusion is a side bias, given a slot that the three main biases do not get.
evidence.c3: One assumed idea (moral status) is argued against e68t9h and ryg483, but those passages state it rather than presuppose it.
evidence.c4: Anchors fit (cke6sj, jnwfxp, pbcr03, xk9gne).
evidence.c5: The three biases (h4mwb2, her4zk, nxxnrj), a major section, are absent, as is the non-Turing dynamics argument.

evidence.c1: Every item is load-bearing.
evidence.c3: The precaution assumption names the exact gap from 'I might be wrong' (qu7j89) to 'nobody should' (yverz7), and extends it via vs0vpj.
evidence.c4: Anchors fit throughout (f87ghx, her4zk, gw0hsq, t54yqa, dgf4em, jvrmrh).
evidence.c5: Has all four arguments including non-algorithmic dynamics, plus the biases, moral status and seeming-vs-being.

evidence.c1: Irreducibility, PCE, pockets, spec-relativity, proof = testing, worth-running, induction and language design are all central.
evidence.c3: 'Toy models generalize' is stated by the author in sx0zyh; the 'visual simplicity as proof' assumption is argued but overstates it, since qexzj4 does justify visual inspection.
evidence.c4: q7khj8 and r32r9j are loose anchors for the toy-model assumption; the introduced anchors fit.
evidence.c5: No idea on unbounded bug rarity (wem6ht) and none on mathematics staying in reducible pockets (whd6dc).

evidence.c1: All load-bearing.
evidence.c3: The only assumed idea ('full predictability makes running pointless') is stated explicitly in nd4kn9 and uqhm5n, so it is not a hidden premise.
evidence.c4: Rarity is anchored to f7mn34 only, missing wem6ht where the busy-beaver claim is made; the rest fit (hcdcqp, zkkrs3, ktzwer).
evidence.c5: Broadest set: adds visual inspection, rarity and mathematics on top of the core.

evidence.c1: Mostly core; the 'randomness vs program' contest is a minor sub-point.
evidence.c3: Both 'assumed' ideas are stated in the text (b9z7g9, wem6ht), and the candidate's own reasoning concedes 'This is actually stated'.
evidence.c4: kk6a0n ('Consider the (3-state, 2-color) Turing machine') and aabpey do not presuppose PCE.
evidence.c5: No mathematics idea and no worth-running paradox.

evidence.c1: All load-bearing; the rind / local-invariant proof is a good catch.
evidence.c3: No assumed ideas are offered, so nothing is laundered but nothing is argued either.
evidence.c4: Good anchors (zbsh70, tgkahp, r7ty6m, vy3nfe); rarity rests on f7mn34 without wem6ht.
evidence.c5: Only one kind of idea, and nothing on mathematics or visual inspection.

evidence.c1: Loop, mixed selectivity, ephaptic coupling, stencils, traveling waves, analog computation and anesthesia are the paper's argument.
evidence.c3: The state-space assumption is tied to xphb7u, ah94dx, ns23sq and qsz9ur as unexplained geometry, which is specific, though it is closer to background vocabulary than to an inferential move.
evidence.c4: Anchors fit (amx5qf, bzqaf5, gkfdys, k02vdw).
evidence.c5: Nothing on the binding/unified-consciousness claim (tdqde5, m9exy5), and no energy-efficiency argument.

evidence.c1: All central; the control-layer idea states the thesis.
evidence.c3: 'Function over substrate' names exactly the inference from wnqgmn to k02vdw; the state-space assumption rests on one anchor.
evidence.c4: Thin: the control layer, stencils and state space each rest on a single anchor (z9g2s3, gxyg0d, ns23sq).
evidence.c5: No consciousness/binding idea; anesthesia appears only as the assumed idea's anchors.

evidence.c1: All load-bearing.
evidence.c3: 'Population geometry is functionally real' is argued against xphb7u, ns23sq and ah94dx, though the article partly argues it itself ('thought to organize').
evidence.c4: Ephaptic coupling is anchored partly on the section heading mapqhv; the rest fit.
evidence.c5: No binding/consciousness idea and no explanation of mixed selectivity via stencils.

evidence.c1: All central.
evidence.c3: 'Consciousness requires unity' precisely targets tdqde5 and m9exy5; the population-code reasoning on x5m34h ('would look like noise') is looser.
evidence.c4: Strong anchors: ectcj5 ties stencils to mixed selectivity, and qr9ra4 to the timing of traveling waves.
evidence.c5: The anesthesia convergence evidence (wnqgmn, k02vdw), the main support for the consciousness claim, is missing.

evidence.c1: Positional status, impersonal respect and Smith's friendship argument are central; the 'innate primate trait' item overstates a point Elias qualifies in k26ath.
evidence.c3: The positional-status assumption is argued across a94czy, f6f8d4, tyj2mt and de69sf; the ritual-performance assumption rests on one quote that states rather than presupposes.
evidence.c4: j3vvp7 is a stretch for 'innate primate' behaviour; hdbtc0 is a loose fit for impersonal respect.
evidence.c5: No idea for the central forecast (k44gdt, zy53n3: relationships are what's left) and none for 'material conditions change what we want' (t4xpae).

evidence.c1: Forecast, clannishness, material conditions, impersonal respect and commerce freeing friendship are all core.
evidence.c3: The case-study assumption is stated explicitly in xcg5en (yet anchored only on c4s3en); the 'stable status needs' assumption leans on cz0cgg, which k26ath qualifies.
evidence.c4: j337dx is a setup sentence rather than a statement of clannishness; the others fit.
evidence.c5: Covers the forecast, method, mechanism, the material-conditions point, respect and friendship.

evidence.c1: All load-bearing; 'removing work removes a dignity system, not the need' captures the thesis.
evidence.c3: The zero-sum status assumption names the unargued step in hdbtc0 and ties it to j3vvp7, tyj2mt and xnesxg.
evidence.c4: The primate item cites k26ath and openly notes the qualification, but still asserts the trait as introduced.
evidence.c5: No 'material conditions change what we want' idea (t4xpae, b3pf45).

evidence.c1: All central.
evidence.c3: The positional-status assumption is argued well via Saint-Simon's precedence rage (x4w0zk); the Junior League anchor (xn6rzj) is looser.
evidence.c4: hb8vvc is a weak anchor for 'material conditions change wants'; the rest fit.

evidence.c1: Structure-to-property, strength/toughness/stiffness, the phase change, feedstock+process and form-follows-function are what the article turns on.
evidence.c3: Form-follows-function names why the gland/use catalogue (m3rk4n, xytxuw) reads as explanation; specific strength names why hng89u's 'five times' is an advantage.
evidence.c4: jzcepa attributes the shortfall to simpler proteins (feedstock), not to process, so it is a stretch for the two-part idea.
evidence.c5: Complete at the right grain for an encyclopedia article, with both kinds of idea.

evidence.c1: Core is covered, but spinning is split into two thin overlapping items (liquid crystal, pulled).

evidence.c4: The pultrusion idea is anchored on ba6knb rather than g2gw42, which actually says it; n5mzfc is only a caption.
evidence.c5: No specific-strength idea.

evidence.c1: Mostly core; 'a gene moved makes the protein' is basic background rather than something this argument turns on.

evidence.c4: The jzcepa reasoning ('implying spinning is the unsolved half') goes beyond what the passage says.

evidence.c1: All central.

evidence.c4: Anchors fit well (b7usb3 for the capture spiral, n7yuqt's RIKEN artificial gland for the process half).

evidence.c1: Cargo cult form, leaning over backwards, don't fool yourself, the Young controls and the ESP shrinkage are the talk's core.
evidence.c3: 'Shrinking effect under tighter controls signals artifact' names the exact move in rbpppq; the g203mu reasoning (selection explains PSI results) is looser.
evidence.c4: s9msxy's viscosity sentence is an honest error, not self-deception; the other anchors fit.
evidence.c5: Nothing on replicating before varying (the tf8rj2 rat student, the m95kqm accelerator), and nothing on institutional pressure.

evidence.c1: All central.

evidence.c5: Nothing on Young's controls or the ignored literature, on publishing both kinds of result, or on institutional pressure.
